ledger.note: 548: Hou Jing takes Shouyang by ambush. 'Southern Yu Province: he took its capital, Shouyang (modern central Anhui), in 548 by ambush.'
548: Hou Jing rebels against the Liang and besieges Jiankang. 'Hou declared a rebellion in summer 548'; 'In winter 548, he arrived at Jiankang and immediately put the capital under siege.'
549: Jiankang falls to Hou Jing. 'Hou now had control of the capital region'; the Wu page: 'In late spring 549, the palace fell to Hou's troops'; Emperor Wu died in the summer.
549: Hou Jing holds Zhejiang. 'by winter 549, Xiao Dalian and the other officials had fallen, which allowed Hou to control most of modern Zhejiang.'
551: Hou Jing takes the throne and proclaims the Han. 'In November 551, Hou Jing had Xiao Dong yield the throne to him'; the Liang page names the regime 'Han' ('In 552, Xiao Yi destroyed Han').

552: the rebellion is over. Hou Jing's head is sent to Xiao Yi at Jiangling.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks: the Hou Jing rebellion held Jiankang's region and most of Zhejiang for three years (spring 549 to May 552) and Shouyang before. cliopatria_names is empty; wikidata null (not checked); the wikipedia field is the Hou Jing article (the Han regime has none). Extents are readings: 'the 13 provinces' as the Henan region; 'the capital region' as a 100 km disc round Nanjing; 'most of modern Zhejiang' as Zhejiang. The pages differ on what came of the northeast: the Hou Jing page has the provinces north of the Yangtze 'largely' surrender to the Eastern Wei after Jiankang fell, the Emperor Yuan page has Hou's generals north of the Yangtze surrender to the Northern Qi in spring 552; the dossiers record both (eastern-wei 549 gain; this loss in 552). Shouyang in 548-552 is the only north-bank land drawn as Hou's. The Gao Huan page is thin: the end of the Henan phase is undated (spring 548 is the Wu of Liang page's date for the collapse). Counterparts: eastern-wei, liang-dynasty, northern-qi (needs a dossier from 550).
